privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.short: This site has no account, no database and no tracking. It asks for nothing about you.
privacy.storage: Your favourites and your Windows / Mac choice are kept in your own browser, on your own device. They never reach a server, they are not shared between your devices, and clearing your browser data erases them.
privacy.cookies: None. What the site keeps is needed to make it work as you asked, so no consent banner is required.
privacy.logs: Vercel, the host, writes technical logs of every visit, which include IP addresses. They serve to run and protect the service. Klacki neither reads nor uses them.
privacy.rights: Since nothing about you is stored on a server, there is nothing to access, correct or delete. To erase what your browser keeps, clear the site data.

sources.title: Sources
sources.intro: Every shortcut is checked against the publisher's own documentation. Here is the page used for each software, with the version and the date it was checked.

about.title: About
about.what: One place for the keyboard shortcuts of creative software: 3D, texturing, VFX, video and 2D. The promise is simple: find a shortcut in under five seconds.
about.how: Shortcuts live in one file per software, checked when the site is built: a wrong or incomplete file stops the build instead of reaching you. Pages are generated ahead of time, so the site stays fast.
about.who: Lucas Nevano, a junior full-stack developer in France. Klacki is a portfolio project.
about.correction: Shortcuts change from one version to the next. If one is wrong, tell me and it gets fixed.

home.lede: Your software, their Windows and Mac keys, read one by one in the publisher's own documentation. The list keeps growing.

trust.text: Every shortcut comes from the publisher's documentation, with its version and the date it was checked. Nothing is copied from another site.

home.demoText: Ctrl does not always become ⌘. Switch Windows / Mac in the header: the keys below are rewritten, straight from the data of the site.

catalogue.title: The software covered
catalogue.lede: One software, one page: its shortcuts sorted by category, its version, and the link to the documentation used as the reference.
catalogue.missingText: Say so, with a link to its official documentation. That is how the list grows.

platforms.title: Windows or Mac, without the traps
platforms.lede: Many lists swap Ctrl for ⌘ automatically. That is wrong half of the time: Blender, Maya and Houdini keep Ctrl on Mac. Here every Mac key is read in the documentation, one by one. Use the toggle above and watch.
platforms.demoTitle: Real shortcuts, taken from the data of this site

rules.title: Ctrl does not always become ⌘
rules.text: Blender, Maya and Houdini keep Ctrl on Mac. Adobe and Foundry software switch to ⌘.

rules.title: Alt is called Option
rules.text: Same physical key, another name. The site shows ⌥ without pretending the shortcut changed.

rules.title: And when the software has no Mac version?
rules.text: Some software is Windows only. Its page says so, and the toggle does not invent a Mac key.

platforms.memo: Your Windows or Mac choice is kept in your browser: you make it once, the site remembers.
